s1.syndrome_frame: A subacute to chronic, asymptomatic, solitary skin lesion
salient_findings: Single asymptomatic lesion on the dorsum of the left hand
Lesion gradually increased in size over 10 months
key_facts: Lesion located on the dorsal aspect of the left hand
Lesion is not adherent to the overlying skin
No history of trauma, discharge, pain, redness, bleeding, or restriction of joint movement
Routine hematologic, liver, and renal function tests are within normal limits

differentials: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath
per_call: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath

shortlist.label: Dermatofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Common, benign skin tumor matching the description of a firm, non-tender nodule

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor of fat cells, possible given the lesion's size and location

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Common, benign cyst that could present as a firm, non-tender nodule

shortlist.label: Pilomatrixoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign skin tumor that could match the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Rare, malignant tumor that should be considered due to the lesion's size and firmness

raw.rationale: The lesion is described as a firm, non-tender, and well-defined nodule, which is consistent with the typical presentation of a dermatofibroma. The lack of adherence to the overlying skin and absence of regional lymphadenopathy also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are typically soft and mobile, which contradicts the firm nature of the lesion in this case

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst
rejected.why: Epidermoid cysts often have a characteristic central punctum and may be transilluminating, which is not mentioned in this case

rejected.label: Pilomatrixoma
rejected.why: Pilomatrixomas are often rock-hard and may have a bluish discoloration, which is not described in this case

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans typically presents as a larger, more irregularly-shaped lesion with a history of gradual growth, and may be adherent to the overlying skin, which is not consistent with this case
